newsitem.title: USA: U.S Southeast power steady on outages, firm demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S Southeast power steady on outages, firm demand.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. held firm Tuesday against Monday's level due to reduced generation availability and return of air-conditioning demand in parts of the region.
"Things are looking pretty strong down here," said a Florida trader.
Bulk power demand in Florida was bolstered by outages of a couple of in-state power plants for seasonal maintenance and scaled back output at another facility, he added.
Hourly prices for electricity among Florida's utilities were assessed in the low $30 range a megawatt hour (MWh).
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Wednesday delivery was pegged near $25.00-$26.00, compared with Monday's $23.50-$25.50.
Firm, off-peak power for next-day delivery at the Ga./Fla. border was notationally valued at $15.00-$16.00.

Up in the northwestern border of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) territory, firm, peak electricity for next day delivery was assessed at $18.00-$19.00, while next-day, off-peak delivery $13.00-$15.00.
Movement of power into northern TVA was heard still in effect because of transmission contraint.
"We have been forced to cut our schedules," said a Southeast trader.
TVA was again absent from making offers in the daily market because of several plant outages which include its 1,148 megawatt (MW) Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Soddy Daisy, Tenn., marketers said.
The possible return of Sequoyah 2 Wednesday would ease the line loading problem in that part of the TVA system, said a Houston marketer.

According to Weather Service Corp, temperatures will run four to eight Fahrenheit degrees above normal on Wednesday in most of the Southeast before a cold front pushes through the region on Friday and Saturday.
